name: Procapil
lead: Procapil is a patented cosmetic ingredient from Sederma (Croda) that combines biotinoyl tripeptide-1, apigenin and oleanolic acid. It is used in hair serums marketed against thinning and shedding. [1]

The supplier claims it anchors follicles, improves scalp microcirculation and limits DHT effects. [1] Human data are small: a sponsor-commissioned placebo-controlled trial and several investigator studies, many combining Procapil with platelet-rich plasma or other ingredients. [1][2][3][4][5]

paras: Grokipedia attributes three actions: oleanolic acid inhibiting 5-alpha reductase, apigenin widening scalp blood vessels, and biotinoyl tripeptide-1 raising adhesion proteins such as collagen IV and laminin 5. It describes these as mostly manufacturer claims. [1]

Grokipedia describes a 4-month placebo-controlled trial commissioned by Sederma in 35 men (3 percent lotion), reporting a roughly 10 percent rise in the anagen-to-telogen ratio versus baseline with no change in placebo; mean growth rate did not change significantly. [1]

A 2023 randomized trial of 54 men found a significantly greater improvement with PRP plus a Redensyl, saw palmetto and biotin product than with PRP plus Procapil. [3] A 2024 quasi-experimental study of 160 patients reported better patient and dermatologist scores at six months for PRP plus 5% Procapil than PRP alone. [5] A 2024 serum study of 32 adults containing Procapil among other ingredients reported increased hair growth rate. [2] A 2024 letter assessed a caffeine plus 3% Procapil formulation in male pattern hair loss. [6] A 2025 review discusses the evidence for Procapil among popular topical ingredients. [4]

Grokipedia reports negative Ames and sensitization tests, and in the PRP comparison study side effects such as itching (18.5 percent), allergic contact dermatitis (14.8 percent) and seborrheic dermatitis (7.4 percent) in the combined-therapy group, which it does not attribute to Procapil alone. [1]

card.summary: A peptide, apigenin and oleanolic acid blend in hair serums; small trials, some sponsor-run, no approved-drug status.
card.note: Most studies combine it with PRP or other actives.

quick.overview:
Procapil is a cosmetic hair-serum ingredient from Sederma. It combines a biotin-linked peptide with apigenin and oleanolic acid.

Small studies report modest changes, but many are sponsor-run or combine it with other treatments.
quick.mechanism: Claimed to anchor follicles, boost scalp microcirculation and reduce DHT effects; these are manufacturer claims per Grokipedia.
quick.risks: Tolerability was good in the 4-month trial described; itching and contact dermatitis were reported in a combined PRP study. It is regulated as a cosmetic, not as a drug.
